name: application-wizard-progress-rail
title: Wizard Progress Rail
description: Vertical wizard navigation rail with connected step circles, per-step title and description, and click-to-jump on completed steps.
useWhen: Building a multi-step setup or onboarding flow laid out with a side rail rather than a horizontal header.
Users benefit from seeing a short description of each step, not just a number or short label.
Completed steps should be directly clickable to jump back, distinct from a purely linear wizard.
avoidWhen: You need a horizontal progress header sitting above a form body — use Stepper Wizard instead, which bundles the header with back/next controls and a content slot.
The flow has no descriptions and only needs a compact numbered/dotted indicator — use Steps instead.
responsiveBehavior: The rail is a single vertical column at all widths; on narrow viewports it typically collapses above the step content rather than sitting beside it.
accessibility: The rail is a <nav> with aria-label, and the current step carries aria-current="step".
Completed steps render as real, keyboard-focusable <button>/<a> elements so jumping back is operable without a mouse.
Upcoming steps are inert (no link or button) rather than disabled interactive elements, since they aren't yet reachable.
The connecting line between steps is aria-hidden decoration; step order and status are conveyed by the list structure and text, not the line alone.

variants.title: Wizard Progress Rail
variants.description: A four-step rail: a completed, clickable 'Account details' step, the current 'Workspace setup' step highlighted, and two upcoming steps in muted gray.
accessibility: Only the completed step is an interactive link; the current and upcoming steps are non-interactive text.

variants.title: Wizard Progress Rail (Dark)
variants.description: The same four-step rail adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Circle borders, connecting lines, and muted upcoming-step text remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
